Title: Full recursive source capture
Requirement: The system shall walk the entire source tree recursively and record every encountered file as a row in MANIFEST.csv.
Rationale: Realizes SN-001; no source file may be silently dropped. AMENDED 2026-08-24 (kit-bump rev6): the recursive walk includes hidden, system and dot-prefixed entries (SR-057) - the 2026-08-24 D-4 finding that no Get-ChildItem call used -Force, so such files and directories were silently skipped.
AcceptanceCriteria: Given a known source tree, every file path (including nested, Unicode, and bracketed names) appears exactly once in the backup MANIFEST.csv after a run.

Title: xxHash128 content hashing
Requirement: The system shall compute each file's content hash with System.IO.Hashing.XxHash128, emitting a 32-char uppercase hex string, deterministically for identical bytes.
Rationale: Realizes SN-001/SN-002; the hash is the identity used for change detection and dedup (see AGENTS.md sec.3).
AcceptanceCriteria: Hashing the same bytes twice yields the same 32-char uppercase hex; different bytes yield a different value (Unit: Get-FileXxHash).

Title: Content dedup by (hash size)
Requirement: The system shall store exactly one physical data file per (xxH2Hash, Length) key - across runs AND within a single run - and record additional logical names as duplicates referencing that data. Where the members of a (hash, Length) group disagree about the stored form, one member shall be elected owner and its form shall define the single object every member references.
Rationale: Realizes SN-002; dedup key is (xxH2Hash, Length) per AGENTS.md sec.3. The within-run clause and the owner-election rule were added at WP9 (D-5): the lookup consulted only the PRIOR backup, so identical files first seen in one run were each stored in full - see SR-060.
AcceptanceCriteria: Two source files with identical bytes produce one stored data file - whether the second is first seen in a later run or in the same run as the first; the manifest marks the second row Duplicate and both resolve to the same data on restore; a group whose members differ in extension or compressibility still yields exactly one physical object.

Title: Selective 7-Zip compression
Requirement: When CompressEnabled is true the system shall store data files as .7z (with a .7z extension) except for already-compressed extensions, keeping the Compressed column consistent with the stored filename.
Rationale: Realizes SN-003; the filename must not lie about compression or hash-recovery breaks (AGENTS.md sec.3, history Mirror+Compress bug).
AcceptanceCriteria: With compression on, a compressible file is stored .7z and Compressed=true; an already-compressed extension is stored verbatim and Compressed=false; the stored filename's extension and the row's Compressed column agree for every stored object (Unit: Test-ShouldCompress).

Title: Dated point-in-time snapshot
Requirement: When a run changes the backup manifest state relative to the prior completed backup — any added, removed, or content/metadata-changed row, including a duplicate-content add served by dedup reuse and a removal whose bytes remain shared — the system shall write a snapshot folder named for the superseded backup's completion date (Snapshot_<date>), made visible only after its manifest is written (rename-on-complete, name matching ^Snapshot_\d{4}_\d{2}_\d{2}_\d{2}_\d{2}_\d{2}), and shall create no snapshot for a manifest-identical (no-op) run nor for the latest live state.
Rationale: Realizes SN-004 and SN-013 crash-safety (B7); the live backup root is itself the latest snapshot, so only superseded states get a folder. 2026-07-02 review: the supersession criterion is a manifest diff, not physical byte I/O — a dedup-served add or shared-content removal still supersedes the prior state.
AcceptanceCriteria: After a change run a folder matching ^Snapshot_\d{4}_\d{2}_\d{2}_\d{2}_\d{2}_\d{2} exists carrying its own MANIFEST.csv; a run whose only change is a duplicate-content add or a shared-content removal still produces a snapshot of the prior state; a manifest-identical no-op run adds no snapshot; same-second collisions get a disambiguator; the folder is never half-populated without its manifest.

Title: Refcount-aware eviction
Requirement: The system shall move a removed file's data out of the live backup only when no remaining manifest row references that (hash, size); shared data shall be retained.
Rationale: Realizes SN-004/SN-002; prevents deleting data still referenced by a duplicate (regression B9).
AcceptanceCriteria: Removing one of two identical files retains the shared data; removing the last reference evicts it to the change folder.

Title: Self-contained restore kit
Requirement: Each run shall deposit a self-contained restore kit (Reconstruct.ps1, reconstruct.sh, FileBackup.Common.psm1, System.IO.Hashing.dll, RECONSTRUCT.paths.json, RECONSTRUCT.bat) into the backup folder and every dated snapshot, and FileBackup.Common shall never depend on FileBackup.Engine. AMENDED 2026-08-24 (kit-bump rev6): kit revision 6, bumped together in both Reconstruct.ps1 and bash/reconstruct.sh (verify-after-write SR-056, locator reclassification SR-040, -Force pool scan SR-057, -NonInteractive guard SR-016); a snapshot keeps the restore kit it was written with (AGENTS.md sec.3), and -Action Verify -RefreshKits is the upgrade path for an existing store.
Rationale: Realizes SN-005; restore must need nothing but the backup folder (AGENTS.md sec.2 load-bearing split).
AcceptanceCriteria: The live backup and each snapshot contain all six kit artifacts; static inspection shows Common imports nothing from Engine.

Title: Bit-exact restore from backup alone
Requirement: Reconstruct shall rebuild the source tree byte-for-byte using only the backup folder's contents, decompressing .7z data and recovering blank-DataPath rows by content hash, without any repo or NuGet install.
Rationale: Realizes SN-005; this is the core promise of the tool.
AcceptanceCriteria: Restoring a backup (incl. compressed and hash-fallback rows) on a clean environment reproduces every original file with identical bytes.

Title: Reject restore target inside backup
Requirement: Reconstruct shall refuse to restore into a target directory located inside the backup folder, and shall refuse any manifest row whose restored destination resolves outside the restore target root (path traversal), counting such a row unrestored.
Rationale: Realizes SN-005 safety; restoring onto the source data would corrupt the backup, and a ..-escaping RelativePath must not write above the target (2026-07-03 bash-v1 reviewer MINOR, fixed on the PowerShell side 2026-08-12).
AcceptanceCriteria: Pointing the restore at a path within the backup folder is rejected with a clear error and no files written; a manifest row whose RelativePath escapes the target root is refused, counted unrestored, and the run fails loudly per SR-029.

Title: Point-in-time restore from a dated snapshot
Requirement: Reconstruct launched from a dated snapshot folder shall treat that snapshot's own manifest as the authoritative file set and resolve each file's bytes by (xxH2Hash,Length) from the data pool (live backup root + all snapshot folders), reproducing that point-in-time state byte-for-byte, without overlaying any newer manifest.
Rationale: Realizes SN-006; fixes the defect where reconstruct overlaid the backup root as newest authority and returned current content for modified files.
AcceptanceCriteria: Restoring Snapshot_<date-of-N> yields every file at its as-of-N version (modified files at their old bytes); restoring the backup root yields the latest state; both are byte-exact.

Title: Deterministic rehash scheduling
Requirement: The system shall decide whether to re-hash an unchanged file from HashRecalcFreq codes A/E/D/W/M/Y/N via Test-HashRecalcDue, deterministically for a given reference time, persisting the last hash-run time in FileBackupState.json.
Rationale: Realizes SN-007; B2/B3/B4 made scheduling real and injectable via -Now.
AcceptanceCriteria: For each code, Test-HashRecalcDue returns the documented decision for a fixed -Now and persisted last-run; A/E always recalc, N never, D/W/M/Y on boundary crossings (Unit + G6).

Title: StoredAsHashSize is the constant 'Hash'
Requirement: Every manifest row the system writes shall carry StoredAsHashSize='Hash', the column recording that the row's data file is named by its content. The legacy value 'Original' shall never be written, and a row carrying it identifies a pre-WP9 path-addressed store, which SR-061 refuses.
Rationale: Realizes SN-008; lets restore know how data files are named. Amended at WP9 (SR-058): with Mirror deleted there is one layout, so the column is a constant rather than a mode indicator - it is kept in the 9-column manifest contract because both restorers and every existing store still read it.
AcceptanceCriteria: After any run every row of MANIFEST.csv carries StoredAsHashSize='Hash' - new, adopted and evicted rows alike - and no code path writes 'Original'.

Title: Independent multi-set processing
Requirement: The system shall process each BackupSet independently such that one set's failure does not abort the others, and the overall exit code shall be non-zero if any set failed.
Rationale: Realizes SN-009 and SN-011; a multi-set scheduled job must be resilient and honest about partial failure.
AcceptanceCriteria: Given multiple sets where one fails, the others still complete and the process exits non-zero.

Title: Optional non-fatal mail
Requirement: The system shall send a success/failure email only when SMTP is fully configured and -NoMail is not set, and shall treat any mail failure as a logged warning that never changes the backup's success status.
Rationale: Realizes SN-010/SN-020 (B15); mail is never load-bearing.
AcceptanceCriteria: With SMTP omitted or -NoMail, no mail is sent and the run proceeds; a send failure is logged WARN and does not flip exit code.

Title: Non-interactive automation safety
Requirement: The system shall provide a -NonInteractive path that never blocks on a prompt during a scheduled run and fails loudly with a non-zero exit on error. AMENDED 2026-08-24 (kit-bump rev6): extend to the restore entry point - Reconstruct.ps1 invoked without -TargetRoot under -NonInteractive (or with input redirected) shall print usage and exit 2 rather than prompting, matching reconstruct.sh's required --target-root.
Rationale: Realizes SN-011; a hanging scheduled task is a silent backup failure.
AcceptanceCriteria: Under -NonInteractive, dependency resolution returns/raises without any Read-Host; a missing optional tool degrades to absent and a fatal condition yields a non-zero exit.

Title: Stale staging guard
Requirement: The system shall abort a run with a clear error when a leftover Temp staging folder exists under ChangePath, rather than proceeding.
Rationale: Realizes SN-013; a stale Temp means a prior run died mid-flight.
AcceptanceCriteria: With a pre-existing Temp folder under ChangePath, the run aborts with a message naming the stale folder and writes no change folder.

Title: Missing config fails clearly
Requirement: The system shall throw a clear error and exit non-zero when the configured config file does not exist, performing no destructive action.
Rationale: Realizes SN-014.
AcceptanceCriteria: Invoking with a non-existent ConfigPath throws "config not found" and exits non-zero; nothing is written to any target.

Title: Required-dependency enforcement
Requirement: The system shall ensure System.IO.Hashing.XxHash128 is available (preferring a bundled DLL) before hashing and shall fail with remediation guidance on an unsupported runtime or missing library.
Rationale: Realizes SN-015; hashing must never silently run against a wrong/absent library (AGENTS.md sec.4, history).
AcceptanceCriteria: On a session lacking the library, Initialize-XxHashLibrary loads the bundled DLL or fails with guidance (non-interactive path throws with remediation); PowerShell <7 is flagged.

Title: External-tool enforcement and degradation
Requirement: The system shall fail before backup processing when compression is selected but 7-Zip cannot be resolved, and shall skip optional media metrics when ffprobe is absent.
Rationale: Realizes SN-016; the manifest must never claim raw bytes are compressed.
AcceptanceCriteria: Without 7-Zip, a compression-enabled run exits non-zero before processing any set; without ffprobe, MediaMBPerSec is left blank.

Title: Literal path safety
Requirement: All file operations shall use -LiteralPath / [System.IO.Path] APIs so Unicode, bracketed, and parenthesized names are handled correctly and never wildcard-expanded.
Rationale: Realizes SN-017; Split-Path -LiteralPath -Parent/-Leaf throws on PS7 (AGENTS.md sec.4).
AcceptanceCriteria: A source tree containing Unicode and [bracketed]/(paren) names backs up and restores with names intact.

Title: Root-only infrastructure filtering
Requirement: The system shall classify infrastructure files (MANIFEST.csv, RECONSTRUCT.*, kit files) only at the backup root via Test-IsInfrastructureFile and shall treat identically-named nested user files as real data.
Rationale: Realizes SN-018 (regression B6).
AcceptanceCriteria: A nested user file named MANIFEST.csv is backed up and restored as data; root-level kit files are excluded from the source manifest (Unit + G1).

Title: Restore capacity check
Requirement: Reconstruct shall verify sufficient free space at the restore target — accounting for the decompressed size of compressed rows — and surface an insufficient-capacity condition before producing a partial tree.
Rationale: Realizes SN-019 (B10/B11).
AcceptanceCriteria: A target without room is rejected with a capacity error; the check uses decompressed sizes for .7z rows.

Title: Idempotent deterministic re-run
Requirement: An identical re-run with no source changes shall produce identical manifest rows and no spurious change content, verified by a deterministic spot check.
Rationale: Realizes SN-021; protects against churn and proves determinism (G7).
AcceptanceCriteria: Two consecutive no-change runs yield byte-identical manifest rows and an empty/no-op change set; a SHA-256 spot check matches.

Title: Manifest schema round-trip
Requirement: The 9-column manifest (DataPath, RelativePath, Length, LastWriteTimeStr, xxH2Hash, Compressed, StoredAsHashSize, Duplicate, MediaMBPerSec) shall be read/written only via Read-Manifest/Write-Manifest, preserving typed Length and LastWriteTime and tolerating null/empty record sets.
Rationale: Realizes SN-005/SN-001; the manifest is the contract restore relies on (AGENTS.md sec.3 invariant).
AcceptanceCriteria: Write-then-read round-trips rows with typed Length/LastWriteTime; a null/empty set is tolerated; a missing manifest reads as @() (Unit).

Title: Cross-change duplicate collapse
Requirement: After a run the system shall collapse duplicate data shared across change folders (Optimize-ChangeFolders) so prior-version history does not store the same bytes repeatedly.
Rationale: Realizes SN-002 within SN-004 history; keeps change history space-efficient.
AcceptanceCriteria: Identical prior-version content across change folders is stored once and still restorable from each referencing change folder.

Title: Dated-snapshot storage and clean cutover
Requirement: The system shall store per snapshot the full point-in-time manifest plus only the bytes superseded at the next run, resolving all other bytes by hash from the live backup or sibling snapshots, and new code shall read and write only the dated-snapshot format (no Pre_*_Changes dual-format handling).
Rationale: Realizes SN-004 with dedup preserved (the manifest carries xxH2Hash); the clean cutover keeps the restore path simple. Pre-existing Pre_* backups still restore via their own bundled kit.
AcceptanceCriteria: A snapshot folder physically stores only superseded data files; unchanged files restore by hash from the pool; the engine and Reconstruct.ps1 contain no Pre_*_Changes naming or reading logic.

Title: First-run setup and discoverable docs
Requirement: The system shall ship a config builder (CredSetEx.ps1) and README quick-start such that a new user can create a valid config and run a first backup, with required dependencies installed on first use.
Rationale: Realizes SN-012; onboarding must not require reverse-engineering the config schema.
AcceptanceCriteria: Following the README quick-start with CredSetEx.ps1 yields a working config and a successful first backup; System.IO.Hashing is auto-installed on first run.

Title: Restore fails loudly on unrecoverable content
Requirement: Reconstruct.ps1 shall restore every recoverable manifest row, log each row it cannot restore (missing data file, failed hash recovery, failed extraction), and terminate with an error (non-zero exit for a scripted caller) stating the count of unrestored files; a fully successful restore shall exit zero. AMENDED 2026-08-24 (kit-bump rev6): ContentMismatch (SR-056) - a restored file whose written bytes do not verify against the manifest and cannot be healed by one pool-recovery attempt - is an unrestored cause under this requirement, counted and named exactly like a missing data file or a failed hash recovery.
Rationale: A silent partial restore defeats the backup's purpose; scheduled/scripted restores check only the exit code (2026-07-02 adversarial-review finding).
AcceptanceCriteria: Deleting a restored row's only data source then restoring yields: every other row restored byte-exact, a log line per failure, and a terminating error naming the unrestored count; an untampered restore completes cleanly with exit 0.

Title: Cross-implementation hash conformance
Requirement: The bash implementation shall compute file content hashes whose output is byte-for-byte identical to Get-FileXxHash: canonical XXH128 (XXH3-128) rendered as a 32-char uppercase big-endian hex string, verified against shared golden fixtures.
Rationale: The (xxH2Hash,Length) key is the identity for dedup, change detection, and hash recovery; any digest mismatch silently breaks cross-implementation restore (2026-07-03 scope change).
AcceptanceCriteria: For each golden fixture file (empty, 1-byte, text, binary >1 MiB, unicode name), the bash hasher's output equals the committed Get-FileXxHash value exactly.

Title: Standalone bash restore
Requirement: reconstruct.sh shall rebuild a source tree byte-for-byte on Linux using only the backup folder's contents plus commodity tools (bash, GNU coreutils/awk, xxhsum, 7z when compressed), honoring the same semantics as the PowerShell restorer: backup-root restores the latest state, a Snapshot_<date> folder restores that point in time from its own manifest (no newer-manifest overlay), blank/missing DataPath rows recover by (xxH2Hash,Length) from the data pool (backup root + all snapshots), .7z rows are decompressed, the restore refuses a target inside the backup, checks capacity, and fails loudly (non-zero exit naming the unrestored count) when any row cannot be restored.
Rationale: Restore-anywhere is the backup's core promise (SN-005/SN-022); Linux is the natural restore host for a NAS or rescue environment (2026-07-03 scope change).
AcceptanceCriteria: A backup produced by the PowerShell engine (each storage mode, ±compression) copied to a Linux machine restores byte-exact via reconstruct.sh from the backup root and from each snapshot; a tampered backup exits non-zero naming the unrestored files.

Title: Manifest portability across platforms
Requirement: The bash implementation shall interpret manifests exactly as written by the Windows engine: RelativePath backslash separators mapped to '/', LastWriteTimeStr parsed as ISO 8601 round-trip ('O') culture-invariantly, CSV fields per RFC 4180 (quoted fields may contain commas/quotes), and UTF-8 content (including BOM tolerance and unicode/bracket/space filenames).
Rationale: The manifest is the cross-platform contract; a parsing divergence corrupts restores silently (2026-07-03 scope change).
AcceptanceCriteria: Golden manifests written by Write-Manifest (incl. unicode, bracketed, comma-containing names) parse to identical field values on Linux; separator mapping round-trips every RelativePath.

Title: Bash backup engine parity
Requirement: The bash backup engine shall produce backups conforming to the same on-disk contract as the PowerShell engine — 9-column MANIFEST.csv, (xxH2Hash,Length) dedup with one physical data file per key, content-addressed short names per the shared alphabet when HashAddressed, extension-gated .7z compression, dated Snapshot_<date> supersession per SR-005, refcount-aware eviction — such that either implementation can restore what the other produced.
Rationale: Full parity lets Linux hosts run scheduled backups against the same targets (SN-023); interop is the anti-duplication guarantee that the contract, not the code, is the single source of truth.
AcceptanceCriteria: A backup produced by backup.sh restores byte-exact via RECONSTRUCT.ps1 on Windows and reconstruct.sh on Linux, and vice versa; snapshot/dedup/no-op semantics match the SR-005/SR-028 acceptance criteria.

Title: Container build and distribution
Requirement: The repository shall provide a non-root Linux container, a portable JSON configuration contract with a writable source-state path distinct from the read-only source, and one command that builds and smoke-tests a compressed backup plus byte-exact restore; the same image shall be exportable as an offline tar or publishable/pullable by fully-qualified OCI registry reference.
Rationale: Lets HomeHub consume the existing engine without a host PowerShell dependency while preserving an offline installation path and keeping registry choice optional.
AcceptanceCriteria: On a Docker-capable Linux runner, Invoke-Container.ps1 -Action BuildAndTest builds the pinned image, reads a read-only source while storing its hash cache on the state mount, creates a compressed backup with the complete recovery kit, restores it in a second container, and byte-compares every source file; Export produces a docker-loadable tar and Publish/Pull use an explicit registry image reference.

Title: Run-state integrity gate
Requirement: When an existing backup's MANIFEST.csv contains rows but its FileBackupState.json is missing or unparseable, the system shall refuse to mutate that backup and exit non-zero rather than treating the run as a first backup.
Rationale: A null prior-backup date routed the run down the first-backup path, which deletes the staged superseded history (HomeHub cross-check finding F, fixed 2026-08-12).
AcceptanceCriteria: With manifest rows present and the state file removed or corrupted between two runs, the second run exits non-zero, changes neither backup bytes nor MANIFEST.csv, and creates no snapshot.

Title: Empty-source delete-all refusal
Requirement: When a previously populated source enumerates zero files, the system shall refuse the run before any backup mutation unless the set explicitly opts in with AllowEmptySource=true; an initially empty source remains valid.
Rationale: An unavailable or mis-mounted source otherwise reads as delete-everything and empties the live backup (HomeHub cross-check finding G, fixed 2026-08-12; mirrors HomeHub's INGEST_ALLOW_EMPTY).
AcceptanceCriteria: With prior manifest rows and an empty source, the run exits non-zero leaving backup bytes and manifest untouched; with AllowEmptySource=true the intentional delete-all proceeds and snapshots the prior state.

Title: Cross-platform tool discovery
Requirement: No tool location shall be constructed from Windows-only environment at module scope; 7-Zip shall resolve from the set's Tools.SevenZipPath configuration or the FILEBACKUP_7ZIP_PATH environment override so the modules import and run on non-Windows hosts.
Rationale: Join-Path $env:ProgramFiles at module scope threw at Import-Module time on Linux, so the tool could not start at all (HomeHub cross-check finding 0, fixed 2026-08-12).
AcceptanceCriteria: Importing FileBackup.Common on a host without $env:ProgramFiles succeeds; a compression-enabled run resolves 7-Zip from Tools.SevenZipPath or FILEBACKUP_7ZIP_PATH and the missing-tool error names both knobs.

Title: Manifest witness sidecar
Requirement: Every MANIFEST.csv the system writes shall be accompanied by a witness sidecar MANIFEST.csv.meta in the same folder, written after the manifest and published by atomic rename, carrying a format version, the manifest's data-row count, its byte length, and the xxHash128 of its bytes exactly as written; the sidecar shall be produced by the single Write-Manifest code path (so backup root, staging, dated snapshots, the source hash cache, and every manifest rewrite are covered), and shall be classified as root-level infrastructure per SR-022 — an identically named nested user file remains data (B6).
Rationale: A restore can only verify the rows its manifest still contains, so a truncated or replaced manifest shrinks the job and still reports success (HomeHub cross-check finding E); a dedup-aware physical file census cannot close this. One writer, one witness, so it cannot drift.
AcceptanceCriteria: After any run, every folder holding a MANIFEST.csv also holds a MANIFEST.csv.meta whose Rows equals the manifest's data-row count, Bytes its file length, and XxH128 the Get-FileXxHash of its bytes; a dated snapshot carries its OWN witness (not the backup root's); a root-level MANIFEST.csv.meta produces no orphan/not-in-DB warning while a nested sub\MANIFEST.csv.meta is backed up and restored as data.

Title: Restore verifies the manifest witness
Requirement: Before restoring any file, Reconstruct.ps1 and bash/reconstruct.sh shall validate the restore origin's manifest: the CSV header shall carry the schema's key columns, and when a MANIFEST.csv.meta is present the manifest's byte length, data-row count, and xxHash128 shall be checked against it — a byte-length or digest mismatch, or an unparseable sidecar, shall abort with the witness exit code before any file is written, while a row-count-only disagreement (byte length and digest both matching) shall warn and proceed because the digest is authoritative. Verification shall run before the target folder and the restore log are created, so a refusal leaves the target untouched. A missing sidecar (a backup written before this contract) shall log an explicit unverified-index warning and continue, unless the caller opts into strict mode (-RequireWitness / --require-witness), which makes absence an abort. An unrecognized sidecar format version shall verify only the fields it understands and warn.
Rationale: Realizes SN-025 and subsumes the 2026-07-03 reviewer MINOR (a corrupt non-CSV MANIFEST.csv restored nothing yet exited 0 in Reconstruct.ps1): an unrecognizable header fails the header check first whatever the file's provenance, and the digest catches damage that preserves the header shape. Refusing legacy backups outright would strand every backup written before this change.
AcceptanceCriteria: A backup whose MANIFEST.csv is truncated or byte-edited aborts both restorers with the witness code 3, and one replaced by unrelated/garbage text aborts with the precondition code 2 — an unrecognizable header is not a manifest at all, so the header check speaks first (precedence 2 > 3); in every refusal NOTHING is written into the target (no restored row and no restore log), because verification runs before the target folder is created; re-stamping the witness makes the same manifest restore cleanly; a witness that disagrees only in Rows (byte length and digest matching) restores with a warning; an origin with no sidecar restores byte-exact and logs 'unverified'; the same origin under strict mode aborts.

Title: Shared restore exit-code contract
Requirement: Both restorers shall report outcome through one documented exit-code table — 0 complete; 1 incomplete because content is unrecoverable; 2 usage or precondition failure (bad arguments, missing or unrecognizable manifest, target inside the backup, missing required tool, insufficient capacity); 3 manifest-witness verification failure; 4 incomplete because of the host (an unreadable or absent search folder, 7-Zip unavailable for an archive candidate, an extraction or copy I/O error) — applying the precedence 2 > 3 > 4 > 1. Hash recovery shall report its failure cause distinctly (content not found, dependency unavailable, storage unreadable, candidate error) rather than one warning for all four, and the terminating summary shall name the count per class. Reconstruct.ps1 shall keep its terminating-error behavior for in-process callers and additionally exit with the table's code when invoked as a process entry point (RECONSTRUCT.bat). AMENDED 2026-08-24 (kit-bump rev6): the locators shall never report a candidate-expansion failure as a host cause - an archive candidate in the pool that does not yield the row's payload is data damage, so the outcome is ContentMissing (1) with the failed candidates named in the detail; a candidate that cannot be read is a host condition and shall be reported as StorageUnreadable (4); a candidate that could not be read shall record one cause, not CandidateError plus DependencyMissing. Restore-loop failures on a row's own file (extraction/copy I/O) remain host-class (4), unchanged. ContentMismatch (SR-056) is added to the content-class cause list. Acceptance: one unrelated garbage .7z in the pool yields exit 1, not 4. AMENDED 2026-08-24 (independent review): an expand failure counts as data damage only after 7-Zip passes a host SELF-TEST (compress+expand a probe); a 7-Zip that cannot run or write is DependencyMissing (4) - the candidate is untested, not disproven. New host-class cause WriteMismatch: a hash-proven pool source whose written destination disagrees.
Rationale: Realizes SN-026 and IF-001's promise of a translatable exit status: today Find-DataFileByHash collapses four causes into one warning and Reconstruct.ps1 throws one generic failure for every cause (HomeHub cross-check finding D). Adopting bash/reconstruct.sh's existing 0/1/2 scheme avoids a competing numbering. Prerequisite for IF-001 leaving Experimental.
AcceptanceCriteria: Every failure cause maps to its documented exit code in both restorers (0 complete; 1 content unrecoverable; 2 usage/precondition; 3 witness-mismatch; 4 host condition); the same damaged store yields the same exit code from Reconstruct.ps1 and reconstruct.sh; exit 0 only when every row restored. [Field restored 2026-08-24: row had been missing AcceptanceCriteria, shifting Permutations..Phase one column left; content unchanged otherwise.]

Title: Backup-side failure aggregation
Requirement: Move-RemovedFilesToStaging and Save-SupersededData shall not abort the run on the first failed move: each failure shall be caught, logged as an ERROR naming the file and cause, and recorded, the loop shall continue with the remaining entries, and the run shall report overall failure (non-zero exit) with a summary count — mirroring Invoke-BackupFileGroup's existing per-entry handling and the restore side's unrestored aggregation.
Rationale: One failed move currently escapes Invoke-BackupSet, hiding every other failure, skipping snapshot finalization, and leaving the Temp staging folder behind so the NEXT run aborts on the SR-017 stale-staging guard (HomeHub cross-check finding J).
AcceptanceCriteria: With two data files made unmovable during one run, the log records an ERROR per failure plus a summary count, every movable entry is still staged, the snapshot is still finalized, the run exits non-zero, no Temp staging folder survives, and the next run proceeds normally.

Title: Versioned JSON configuration contract
Requirement: The JSON configuration shall be a versioned, closed schema validated before any dependency initialization or backup mutation: a required integer ConfigVersion (currently 2; version 1 is refused as TOO OLD - its key set carried the removed PreserveFolderTree selector); a BackupSets array of at least one object each requiring non-empty Name, SourcePath, BackupPath, ChangePath, a HashRecalcFreq in {A,E,D,W,M,Y,N} (case-insensitive), and a JSON-boolean CompressEnabled, with optional SourceStatePath (default SourcePath), AllowEmptySource (default false), BrowseView (off|index, default off) and ViewPath (default <BackupPath>_View); optional Tools.SevenZipPath / Tools.FfprobePath and optional Secrets.{ToEmail,FromEmail,SmtpServer,SmtpPort}. Any key not in the schema, any value of the wrong JSON type, a missing or unparseable ConfigVersion, a ConfigVersion outside the supported range, or a Secrets.Credential key shall abort the run with a terminating error naming the offending key by its JSON path and the expected type or value set. A JSON config declaring more than one BackupSets entry shall log a warning naming the count and referencing IF-001's one-set-per-invocation ruling. The CLIXML configuration shall remain supported as the unversioned legacy native-Windows form, subject to the same per-set shape checks but exempt from the version, closed-schema, and credential rules. Type checking shall cover EVERY schema-defined value, not only the two booleans: each required and optional string (Name, SourcePath, BackupPath, ChangePath, HashRecalcFreq, SourceStatePath, Tools.SevenZipPath, Tools.FfprobePath, Secrets.ToEmail/FromEmail/SmtpServer) shall be a JSON string, each boolean (CompressEnabled, AllowEmptySource) a JSON boolean, and Secrets.SmtpPort a JSON integer, since PowerShell's coercions would otherwise change the document's meaning ([bool]'false' is true, so a quoted "false" for AllowEmptySource disarms the SR-036 delete-all refusal; [string] of an array joins it, so ["x","y"] becomes the literal path 'x y'). Because JSON has a single number type, an integral-valued number is that integer (ConfigVersion 2.0 is 2); a ConfigVersion outside the supported range shall be refused as an unsupported version, not as a malformed number. A single bare BackupSets object shall be accepted and wrapped, and container/FileBackup.schema.json shall express the same rule. A configuration carrying the removed PreserveFolderTree key shall be refused BY NAME rather than by the generic unknown-key message, in every configuration format including CLIXML (SR-063).
Rationale: IF-001's import half was under-specified: the JSON branch was a bare ConvertFrom-Json with no schema, no version field and no test, so a mistyped key was silently ignored (AllowEmptySource defaults to false when absent, disarming the delete-all refusal by accident) and a quoted "false" was coerced true by [bool], enabling compression against the operator's intent. This is the remaining blocker to IF-001 leaving Experimental.
AcceptanceCriteria: container/FileBackup.example.json validates unmodified and, with only its five path fields and Tools.SevenZipPath retargeted, drives a real backup that restores byte-exact; each of missing ConfigVersion, ConfigVersion=3, ConfigVersion=1, unknown top-level key, unknown per-set key, string "false" for CompressEnabled, HashRecalcFreq='Q', empty BackupSets, non-integer SmtpPort, and Secrets.Credential is refused before any file is created, with the offending key named in the message; an omitted AllowEmptySource yields false and an omitted SourceStatePath yields SourcePath; the same CLIXML configs used by the existing suites still load unchanged. In addition each of a quoted "false" for AllowEmptySource, an array SourcePath or HashRecalcFreq, a numeric Name, SourceStatePath, Tools.SevenZipPath or Secrets string, a ConfigVersion out of range, and an unknown Tools key is refused naming the key with the set's real index; the published schema and the runtime validator are driven from ONE shared fixture corpus so they cannot drift; and a refused run creates no artifacts at all, including never creating a log directory and never truncating the previous run's global log.

Title: Configuration failure is distinguishable at the process boundary
Requirement: FileBackup.ps1 shall accept an -ExitCode switch that makes it report through the documented status table when run as a process entry point: 0 for a complete run, 1 when one or more backup sets failed, and 2 when the configuration could not be loaded or violates SR-042 — the same usage/precondition class the restorers use. Without the switch the entry point shall keep its current behavior (terminating error for configuration problems, exit 1 for a failed set) so in-process callers and the existing suites are unaffected. container/entrypoint.sh shall pass -ExitCode so a containerized run's exit status distinguishes a bad configuration from a failed backup. A configuration file that is missing, unreadable, or of an unsupported extension is a configuration failure of the same class and shall report 2 under -ExitCode (it is the likeliest container misconfiguration, and exit 1 would tell a supervisor to retry forever). A refused configuration shall create no artifacts: the global log file shall not be created or truncated until the configuration has passed validation.
Rationale: IF-001 promises HomeHub a translatable exit status, and NagLight must distinguish 'your config is wrong, retrying will not help' from 'the backup failed'; today both surface as exit 1. Complements WP1's restore exit-code table with the same 2 = usage/precondition meaning.
AcceptanceCriteria: Run as a child process with -ExitCode: a schema-violating config returns 2 having created no backup artifacts; a config whose one set fails returns 1; a clean run returns 0; the same invocations without -ExitCode return the pre-change codes and the in-process invocation still throws. A missing config file and an unsupported extension each return 2 under -ExitCode; a refused run leaves a pre-existing global log byte-intact and creates no log directory at a fresh path.

Title: Container distribution and snapshot-restore roundtrip proof
Requirement: CI shall prove, inside the container job, that an exported image reloads via `docker load` into a working image, that publish/pull through a registry produces a working image, and that a second incremental container run produces a dated snapshot that restores byte-exact in-container alongside the latest state.
Rationale: Closes the gap between SR-034's acceptance criteria (which already promises tar/registry distribution and container use) and what CI actually exercises today (BuildAndTest only, single no-snapshot run) -- container-v1 cannot be called released without this.
AcceptanceCriteria: In the `container` CI job: Export -> docker rmi -> Invoke-Container.ps1 -Action Load -> -Action Test all succeed against the reloaded image; Publish to a throwaway registry:2 service -> docker rmi both tags -> -Action Pull -> -Action Test all succeed against the pulled image; the smoke test's kit check lists all 8 real kit artifacts (adds RECONSTRUCT.paths.json); a second, source-mutating container run creates exactly one Snapshot_<date> folder under /changes, and both the post-run latest state and the pre-mutation snapshot restore byte-exact in separate restore containers.

Title: Snapshot pruning re-homes still-referenced bytes before deletion
Requirement: Removing a dated snapshot shall first identify every (xxH2Hash,Length) key that a surviving manifest resolves by hash and whose only physical copy lies inside the snapshot being removed, and shall copy that file byte-for-byte into the surviving pool BEFORE the folder is deleted. The destination shall be where Optimize-ChangeFolders would have elected the keeper had the snapshot never existed: the backup root when the root manifest demands the key, otherwise the newest surviving snapshot that demands it. At that destination one demanding row shall be pointed at the copied file -- DataPath set to the synthesized data-file name and Compressed/StoredAsHashSize adopted from the SOURCE row, because the physical form travels with the bytes and pruning shall never re-pack or re-compress. The name shall be synthesized exactly as Invoke-BackupFileGroup would for that form (Get-HashSizeFileName with '.7z' when compressed else the logical extension; a legacy StoredAsHashSize='Original' row, which prune still serves, keeps the RelativePath plus '.7z' when compressed). No manifest row shall be added, removed or reordered and the six logical columns (RelativePath, Length, LastWriteTimeStr, xxH2Hash, Duplicate, MediaMBPerSec) shall be unchanged everywhere; only DataPath, Compressed and StoredAsHashSize shall ever differ, and only in planned rows. Every manifest the operation rewrites shall be persisted through Write-Manifest so its SR-038 witness is re-stamped, and MANIFEST.csv.meta shall never be copied between folders. The mechanism shall be correct in all four storage modes, and a prune that endangers nothing shall copy nothing.
Rationale: Snapshots share bytes. A blank-DataPath row resolves by (hash,length) from anywhere in the pool, so a folder that looks like old history can hold the only physical copy other snapshots need -- deleting it from outside the tool is silent data loss (HomeHub cross-check finding I, re-ruled 2026-08-21: HomeHub owns retention policy, FileBackup owns the mechanism). Re-homing with an explicit destination DataPath rather than 'copy it anywhere' also avoids unreferenced pool bytes, makes an interrupted run trivially checkable, and closes the finding-C form hazard for the row it touches.
AcceptanceCriteria: Byte-exact restores of every surviving dated state AND the latest state in all four storage modes after pruning the oldest, a middle, the newest and the sole remaining snapshot; re-homed content hashes to its row's xxH2Hash at its row's Length; a column-wise before/after manifest diff is confined to DataPath/Compressed/StoredAsHashSize in planned rows only, with identical row sets; every rewritten manifest verifies against its witness; a prune whose snapshot endangers nothing copies zero bytes; on quiescent states content still exists exactly once per (hash,length).

Title: Snapshot pruning is transactional and refuses loudly
Requirement: Snapshot removal shall run as an ordered transaction whose invariant is that the pool goes redundant before the snapshot disappears, never deficient: (0) preflight with no mutation -- rails, manifests, witnesses, plan, capacity and orphan checks, which is also exactly what -WhatIf reports; (1) materialize each re-homed file by copying to '<destination>.fbprune.tmp' on the same volume, verifying it, and publishing it by atomic rename; (2) publish every touched destination manifest through Write-Manifest; (3) prove that, with the target excluded, EVERY surviving manifest row still resolves -- a non-blank DataPath to a file present in its own folder whose form agrees with its Compressed column, a blank DataPath to a key present in the pool, whose located copies must additionally agree in form only when the row's OWN folder carries a pre-revision-2 restore kit (a revision-2+ kit decides a hash-recovered file's form from the located FILE, SR-050, so a form difference restores correctly and shall not block retention - amended 2026-08-23, WP7) -- aborting with the snapshot intact on any failure; (4) commit by renaming the folder out of the ^Snapshot_ namespace to 'Pruning_<name>' (which fails the pattern used by Reconstruct.ps1, reconstruct.sh and Optimize-ChangeFolders alike, so one atomic rename removes it from every consumer's view) and only then deleting it. The operation shall refuse before mutating anything, each refusal reporting its SR-040 code with batch precedence 2 > 3 > 4 > 1: a manifest whose witness mismatches or is unparseable (3); a manifest with NO witness (3) unless -AllowUnverifiedIndex is passed, the deliberate inverse of the restore default because restoring against an unverified index is recoverable and deleting against one is not; the SR-035 run-state gate (2); an existing Temp staging folder (2), which prune itself holds for its duration with a PRUNE.inprogress marker so a concurrent backup aborts on the existing SR-017 guard with no new code in the backup path; a target that is not an existing ^Snapshot_ folder directly under the resolved change root, or any wildcard (2); data files in the target that its own manifest does not reference (2) unless -DiscardUnreferencedData is passed; a pool that already fails to resolve, or whose located form disagrees with a row's Compressed where that row's folder carries a pre-revision-2 kit (2, naming the rows and the -RefreshKits remedy); insufficient free space at a destination volume (2), measured per destination volume through Common's Get-VolumeIdentity/Get-FreeSpaceBytes (SR-052) so the rail also exists on UNC and POSIX-rooted stores, and skipped rather than refused when a volume cannot be measured; a compressed plan with no usable 7-Zip (2); and a host I/O failure while copying (4, always before the commit point). A refusal shall leave the tree byte-identical, FileBackupState.json included. A refusal shall mutate NOTHING; the single exception, deliberately scoped, is that before the named snapshot is planned the mechanism completes an outstanding 'Pruning_<that same name>' deletion, which is already past the commit point and invisible to every consumer (residue for any other name is left alone). Recovery shall need no journal: re-running the same command recomputes the plan from disk, that name-scoped completion finishes an interrupted commit, and an entry sweep INSIDE the transaction -- after the rails pass and the Temp lock is held, so its failures classify as the retriable 4 -- removes the staged copies left behind, so an interruption at any phase boundary loses nothing. The sweep shall identify residue by the destination manifest, never by the '.fbprune.tmp' suffix alone: a user file stored at a verbatim path that ends in that suffix carries a manifest row and is content, while a staged copy is unreferenced by construction. Under -WhatIf neither the residue completion nor the sweep shall run, so nothing is logged or counted that did not happen. The Temp lock shall be taken by CREATING the directory (no -Force), so creation itself is the atomic test and an already-existing folder is the staging-busy refusal (2).
Rationale: Deleting backup content is the least reversible thing this tool does, so the ordering has to be provable rather than plausible, and every refusal has to be distinguishable by a wrapper (NagLight maps 3 to an integrity ESCALATE, 2 to 'do not retry', 4 to 'retry'). A journal was rejected deliberately: it is a second source of truth that can itself go stale, whereas the plan is always recomputable from the disk.
AcceptanceCriteria: Interrupting the operation at each phase boundary leaves every dated state restorable, leaves residue invisible to both restorers, and a re-invocation completes and sweeps it; each of the ten induced refusals returns its documented code against a tree whose every file is hash-identical before and after, including FileBackupState.json; -AllowUnverifiedIndex and -DiscardUnreferencedData turn their own refusals into warned successes and nothing else; -WhatIf reports the classification and the reclaim figure the real run then achieves. A compression-policy flip on a store whose kits are all revision 2+ prunes successfully and every remaining state still restores byte-exact; the same store with one snapshot's kit regressed below revision 2 refuses form-mismatch, naming the kit revision and -RefreshKits (WP7). A user file whose name ends in '.fbprune.tmp' (root-level and nested) survives a refused prune, a dry run and a successful prune of another snapshot, and still restores byte-exact; a refused prune leaves an interrupted run's residue untouched; -WhatIf leaves it untouched and logs nothing about it; an undeletable committed residue is reported as code 4.

Title: Snapshot inventory with dedup-aware reclaim figures
Requirement: The tool shall report a read-only inventory of the dated snapshots in a store: per snapshot Name, Date, Rows, PhysicalBytes, BytesReclaimed and BytesReHomed, computed from the pooled manifests and the physical content index, mutating nothing. BytesReclaimed shall be what removing that snapshot now would actually free across the whole store -- its physical size less the bytes that must first be re-homed into the surviving pool -- and BytesReHomed shall be that copy cost, both derived from the same plan the real removal executes so the reported figure is the achieved figure by construction. The inventory shall be emitted as objects in-process and as one JSON document at the process boundary.
Rationale: Because of dedup a snapshot folder's size is NOT what deleting it frees, so a wrapper deciding what to keep cannot compute the number itself; and IF-001 requires the retention decision to be made outside FileBackup while the arithmetic stays inside it.
AcceptanceCriteria: The reported BytesReclaimed for each snapshot equals the measured whole-store size drop after actually removing it, and BytesReHomed equals the measured bytes copied; running the report leaves every file in the store byte-identical; the JSON parses to one object per snapshot carrying all six fields.

Title: Retention is invocable at the container boundary
Requirement: FileBackup.ps1 shall accept -Action Backup|Prune|Snapshots (default Backup) and -Snapshot <name[,...]>, resolving the single configured set through Import-BackupConfiguration + Resolve-BackupSetPaths and dispatching to the retention mechanism (with -WhatIf passed through) or to the inventory, whose records are written to stdout as JSON. Under -ExitCode the outcome shall be reported through the SR-040 table (0 pruned / 1 batch incomplete but no data lost / 2 usage or precondition, nothing mutated / 3 manifest-witness verification failed, nothing mutated / 4 host I/O, retriable), precedence 2 > 3 > 4 > 1. container/entrypoint.sh shall dispatch on FILEBACKUP_ACTION (default backup) or a leading positional word in {backup, prune, snapshots}, mapping FILEBACKUP_SNAPSHOT and FILEBACKUP_DRY_RUN onto -Snapshot and -WhatIf; any argument starting with '-' shall pass through to FileBackup.ps1 exactly as today, so existing flag-only invocations are byte-identical in behavior. There shall be NO prune in bash: reconstruct.sh stays restore-only, because pruning must re-stamp manifest witnesses and the bash side has no manifest writer, and pruning is never required in order to restore.
Rationale: HomeHub runs retention as a separate one-shot container invocation per directory (IF-001's one-set-per-invocation ruling), so the mechanism has to be reachable from the entrypoint with the same exit vocabulary as backup and restore -- while every existing container invocation must keep behaving exactly as it does today.
AcceptanceCriteria: In-container: the snapshots action emits parseable JSON and exits 0 while modifying nothing; pruning a valid name exits 0 and every remaining state still restores byte-exact in-container; an unknown name exits 2 with the tree unchanged; a dry run exits 0 changing nothing; the default action and a flags-only invocation behave byte-identically to before (TC-060/TC-076 re-run unchanged); a source guard proves reconstruct.sh carries no removal path.

Title: Storage-form verification and repair
Requirement: The system shall provide an opt-in verification action, never invoked by a normal backup run, that audits every manifest row in the backup root and in every Snapshot_* folder against the physical bytes: the DataPath extension, the Compressed column and the actual stored form of the file must agree; a blank-DataPath row's Compressed must agree with the form of the file the shared restore hash-recovery locates for its (xxH2Hash,Length); and every non-blank DataPath must exist. Verification shall mutate nothing and report each finding with its row, folder and class. An explicit repair mode shall correct only findings that are unambiguous from bytes in the row's own folder - taking the physical bytes as ground truth, rewriting the Compressed column and renaming the data file so name and form agree, never re-packing or re-compressing content, never editing the six logical columns, and persisting every touched folder through Write-Manifest so its SR-038 witness is re-stamped. Repair shall act on the PHYSICAL data file, not on the row: rows deduplicated onto one data file shall be repaired together - the file renamed once and every row that referenced the old path updated to the observed form - so a repair can never leave a sibling row pointing at a path that no longer exists. Findings about blank-DataPath rows shall be reported, never silently repaired. Outcome shall be reported through the SR-040 exit-code table.
Rationale: Realizes SN-030 and closes HomeHub cross-check finding C. As originally found (WP5, before WP9 deleted the migration): Sync-BackupStorageLayout's migration decision compared manifest metadata with configuration and never with the bytes, so a malformed row validated itself, and a transformation that failed on a malformed row was swallowed into a log line without failing the run. Deleting the migration removed that particular writer; it did NOT remove the need for the audit, because nothing else ever compares the index with the bytes either - a wrong Compressed/StoredAsHashSize claim, however it got there (an older build, external damage, a hand-edited manifest), still validates itself forever. A physical verify inside every migration would fight SR-024 idempotence and run-time cost, so the check is a separate opt-in action.
AcceptanceCriteria: A backup seeded with each malformed shape (Compressed=Yes over raw bytes; Compressed=No over archive bytes; a .7z name over raw bytes; a dangling DataPath) is reported by the verification action with one finding per row and a non-zero status, with the tree byte-identical afterwards; repair mode makes each unambiguous case agree and a subsequent verification reports clean; two rows sharing one physical data file are BOTH healed by one repair (the store re-verifies clean and restores byte-exact, with no dangling row); a clean backup verifies clean and exits 0 in all four storage modes; a normal backup run never invokes verification (source-level guard) and a backup run immediately after a repair is idempotent (SR-024).

Title: Restore resolves storage form from the located file
Requirement: When a manifest row's DataPath is blank and its bytes are recovered by (xxH2Hash,Length) from elsewhere in the data pool, both restorers shall decide whether to decompress from the FORM OF THE FILE THEY LOCATED - which the hash-recovery search has already proven, by expanding an archive candidate and matching its payload - and not from the row's Compressed column. A row with a non-blank DataPath shall continue to be resolved by its own Compressed column, which describes the file in its own folder. Where an archive candidate does not yield the row's payload - whether it fails to expand (a .7z name over raw content) or expands SUCCESSFULLY to other content (a genuine .7z SOURCE file, which SR-004 stores raw) - the candidate shall additionally be considered as raw bytes before it is dropped. Both restorers shall behave identically and keep the SR-040 exit-code contract.
Rationale: Realizes SN-030. A blank-DataPath row's Compressed column describes the form the byte had in another folder at another time; consulting it for a file found elsewhere in the pool is reading the wrong field. Reachable with no tampering at all: compression is per-file and per-run (SR-004) and nothing already stored is ever re-formed (SR-061), so a store legitimately holds both forms of unrelated content and a blank row's bytes may live in any folder - a row that says No while the only surviving copy is a .7z then plain-copies archive bytes under the original filename and exits 0 (WP4 retention plan finding F3; homehub cross-check finding C family). Before WP9 the compression-flip migration reached the same state by converting only the backup root and leaving snapshots behind. The located file's form costs nothing to report: Reconstruct.ps1:225-249 and reconstruct.sh:224-245 have already proven it.
AcceptanceCriteria: With compression on or off, a snapshot restored after a compression-policy flip that leaves only the opposite-form copy in the pool reproduces the original bytes exactly and exits 0 in BOTH restorers; the same holds in the reverse direction; a non-blank DataPath row's behaviour is unchanged (TC-021 and G3 remain green); a genuinely unrecoverable row still exits 1 and a host-class failure still exits 4; a blank row for a GENUINE .7z source file - produced by an ordinary timeline with no tampering - restores byte-exact with exit 0 in both restorers.

Title: No run deletes a data file a live row still claims
Requirement: No step of a backup run shall delete or move out of the pool a data file that any row of the final manifest still references, and rows that share one physical data file shall be treated as one unit, so no operation can leave a row pointing at a path that is gone.
Rationale: Dedup makes several rows share one DataPath, so every deletion site needs the reference counting Move-RemovedFilesToStaging already performs (B9). The original wording scoped this to Sync-BackupStorageLayout's migration; WP9 deleted that function (SR-061) and moved the invariant to the two sites that still delete: eviction of removed files, and Save-SupersededData's preservation of superseded bytes - whose old source-based survival test was exactly the D-1 defect (defect review 2026-08-24).
AcceptanceCriteria: Removing either member of a dedup group leaves the survivors' object in the pool and every state restorable byte-exact with exit 0; a superseded object still claimed by a frozen row, or by a row whose replacement copy failed, is retained rather than parked; no data file referenced by the final manifest is missing after any run.

Title: Backup-side capacity preflight
Requirement: Before writing any backup or staging bytes, the engine shall estimate the bytes the run will add to the backup volume (new deduplicated content, sized by uncompressed length, the migration term retired with the migration itself at WP9, SR-061) and to the change volume (superseded and removed content that must be copied rather than renamed because it crosses a volume), compare the demands against free space PER VOLUME - summing both demands against one volume's free space when the two roots resolve to the same volume, since they then compete for the same bytes - and refuse the backup set before mutation when a volume is insufficient, naming the volume, the requirement and the free space. Volume identity shall be taken from the host's mount table (the longest mount point that prefixes the resolved path), so it is a real volume on Linux as well as on Windows and never the path itself. The same free-space measurement shall be used by Reconstruct.ps1, replacing the drive-qualifier lookup that cannot resolve a POSIX path and therefore silently skips the SR-023 check on Linux and in the container.
Rationale: Realizes SN-030 and the backup half of SN-019. SR-023 is restore-only and there is no free-space logic anywhere in the engine (verified at 18e4c98). The destination is a HomeHub-controlled bind mount, so a full volume is a realistic failure mode, and a run that fills the volume mid-way leaves the manifest and the bytes out of step. Reconstruct.ps1:443 resolves capacity through Split-Path -Qualifier, which errors on a rooted POSIX path and is caught by the adjacent handler, so the container restore has no capacity guard at all while bash/reconstruct.sh:508 does.
AcceptanceCriteria: A backup set whose new content exceeds the destination's free space refuses before any file is created; a blank-DataPath row about to be healed (SR-053) contributes its Length to the backup demand - a blank row holds no bytes, so its key must not read as already-held (WP7 review, required change 1) or modified, with the tree byte-identical, a message naming volume/required/free, and a non-zero status; a set that fits proceeds unchanged; two demands that each fit but together exceed one shared volume's free space are refused; the measurement returns a plausible non-zero value for a rooted POSIX path on Linux and for a drive-qualified path on Windows, and the volume identity of a path is a mount point from the host's mount table (so a mount point and a folder inside it are ONE volume); the restore capacity check demonstrably fires on Linux (container) where it previously skipped.

Title: The backup run heals blank-DataPath rows and never adopts them
Requirement: The engine shall treat a backup-root manifest row whose DataPath is blank as CHANGED in the source-to-backup diff whenever the source still carries that RelativePath, so the next run re-establishes real bytes for it: either by copying from the source or by re-pointing at a surviving deduplicated copy. The deduplication step shall never select a row whose DataPath is blank as the "existing content" to adopt - a blank row is damage in the process of being healed, and adopting it hands a new file a row that points at nothing while its bytes are never written. Healing shall be silent-success-safe in the other direction too: a heal changes the manifest, so the run that heals mints its dated snapshot exactly as any other manifest-changing run does.
Rationale: The 2026-08-23 investigation reproduced the un-healed store end-to-end: after an external deletion inside the backup root (AV quarantine, cloud-sync dehydration, an operator tidying), the row was blanked with one WARN and never re-copied although the diff itself proved the source unchanged - and a new same-content file adopted the blank row with zero warnings and no bytes written. The store degraded forever while every run reported success.
AcceptanceCriteria: Deleting a data file inside the backup root leaves the next run exiting 0 with the row pointing at real bytes again (re-copied from the still-matching source, or re-pointed at a surviving dedup copy) and the full tree restoring byte-exact; a new source file whose content matches a blank row gets its own physical bytes and both rows resolve; the pure diff marks a metadata-identical row with a blank DataPath as changed; a run with no blank rows behaves byte-identically to before.

Title: Verification reports rows whose bytes are gone from the pool
Requirement: -Action Verify shall, in addition to the storage-form audit, run the pool-resolution audit (Test-PoolResolves) across the backup root and every snapshot and report each row that no longer resolves to bytes anywhere in the pool as a finding of class PoolUnresolvable in the same JSON findings document, driving the SR-040 findings exit (1). The pool audit always spans the whole pool - a pool is one unit - regardless of the form audit's -BackupRootOnly scoping. These findings are report-only: -RepairStorage shall not claim to repair them (bytes cannot be conjured); the remedy is the next backup run while the source still holds the content, or restoring the content into the pool.
Rationale: The investigation's decisive finding: a store with permanently unrestorable rows verified CLEAN, even under -Deep, because the only check that knew (Test-PoolResolves) ran solely inside prune preconditions. An operator who never prunes got zero signal until the restore they actually needed failed.
AcceptanceCriteria: With every physical copy of one row's content deleted from the pool, -Action Verify exits 1 and its JSON document contains a PoolUnresolvable finding naming the folder and RelativePath; a row whose NAMED data file is gone while the content still survives elsewhere in the pool is reported as the distinct class PoolDataPathMissing, never PoolUnresolvable - it restores via the revision-4+ fallback and heals on the next run, and calling it unresolvable would hand the wrapper a false data-loss alarm (WP7 review, required change 2); a clean store still prints the empty document and exits 0; -RepairStorage leaves the finding reported, not "repaired".

Title: Non-portable filenames are refused loudly at backup time
Requirement: During the source scan - BEFORE any attempt to open or hash the file, since a name Windows cannot open would otherwise abort the whole set on a read error - the engine shall skip any source file one of whose path components is not a legal file name on BOTH platforms: any character Windows forbids (< > : " | ? * and control characters, newline included), a component ending in a dot or space (which Windows strips), a component whose stem (the text before the first dot) is a Windows reserved device name (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-COM9, LPT1-LPT9, case-insensitively, with or without an extension - WP9 step 8b, ruled IN 2026-08-25), or, on a non-Windows host, a component containing a backslash (a path separator to the Windows restorer). Each skipped file shall produce one ERROR naming the file and the offending character, the set shall be marked failed (non-zero exit), every other file shall still be backed up, and no manifest row shall be written for the skipped file. A PREVIOUSLY stored row whose (non-portable) name is still present in the source shall be left frozen - neither re-processed nor treated as removed-from-source and evicted.
Rationale: Human ruling 2026-08-23: the twin-restorer contract (SN-022/SN-026) breaks on such names (7-Zip argument quoting mis-splits a quote, the bash line-based parser cannot read a newline row), and handling them is complexity spent on names the user almost certainly wants fixed at the source. Loud skip retires review findings R6 and R7 at the source for every newly written store.
AcceptanceCriteria: The classification is per component: quotes, pipes, control characters, and trailing dot/space are refused with a reason naming the character; Unicode, brackets, parens, spaces are portable. End-to-end (trailing-dot shape, hostable on Windows via \\?\): the run exits 1 with one Skipping ERROR, writes no row for the bad name, still backs up every other file, and leaves a pre-existing row under that name frozen in the manifest with its data file intact.

Title: Restore verifies the bytes it wrote
Requirement: After restoring any manifest row - expanded or copied, resolved through its own DataPath or hash-recovered - both restorers shall hash the written file and compare (Length, xxH2Hash) against the row; on disagreement the written file shall be deleted, the (hash,length) pool recovery attempted once, and the result verified again; a row that cannot be verified shall be counted into the SR-029 unrestored accounting as the content-class cause ContentMismatch (exit 1), never reported as success. AMENDED 2026-08-24 (independent review): the one recovery attempt applies to a row NOT resolved through the pool locator; a mismatch whose SOURCE was already hash-proven by the locator is a WriteMismatch - a HOST-class outcome (exit 4), because the pool demonstrably holds the bytes and the write is what failed. A written file that cannot be read back for verification is likewise host-class, and the file is kept.
Rationale: Realizes SN-033; the 2026-08-24 HomeHub bench defect review (D-2) found both restorers restore a resolvable DataPath with no hash check - a wrong payload, a same-length bit-flip and a truncated file all exit 0 today.
AcceptanceCriteria: A data file altered to wrong-payload, same-length-bitflip or truncated content restores byte-exact from a surviving pool copy (exit 0, one WARN logged naming the row) when a good copy exists; the row is named in the SR-029 unrestored accounting as ContentMismatch (exit 1) when no good copy exists; an untampered restore is unaffected.

Title: Hidden and dot-prefixed files are captured and located
Requirement: Every filesystem enumeration in the engine, the shared module and the Windows restorer shall include hidden, system and dot-prefixed entries (files and directories) - source walks, the restore pool scan, the snapshot enumerations, the prune residue sweep and the prune byte accounting alike - so that no source file is silently omitted and no pool file is invisible to (hash,length) recovery. Deliberate exclusion is achieved by scoping SourcePath (no per-set exclusion or hidden-file configuration knob exists; the prune-internal ExcludeFolder parameter is not user configuration - wording corrected 2026-08-24 at G3 closure). Reparse-point/symlink traversal semantics are unchanged by this requirement.
Rationale: Realizes SN-001 and SN-031; the 2026-08-24 D-4 finding: no Get-ChildItem anywhere in Engine/Common/Reconstruct used -Force, so hidden and dot-prefixed source files were never backed up, hidden/dot pool files were invisible to restore, and the twin restorers disagreed (bash find never skipped them).
AcceptanceCriteria: A dot-prefixed file, a nested dot-directory, a Windows Hidden file/directory and a System-attribute file all appear in MANIFEST.csv and restore byte-exact in all four storage modes; a dot-named or Hidden pool data file is found by (hash,length) recovery; no new configuration key exists.

Title: Content addressing is the only storage layout
Requirement: Every data file the system stores shall be named by its content via Get-HashSizeFileName ("<hashShort> <sizeShort><ext>"); no configuration shall select a mirrored (path-addressed) layout.
Rationale: Deletes D-1's hazard class structurally rather than guarding it: different content yields a different filename, so a stored object can never be overwritten in place (defect review 2026-08-24; human ruling option 3, 2026-08-24).
AcceptanceCriteria: After any run every non-blank DataPath in MANIFEST.csv matches the hash-name grammar and StoredAsHashSize is 'Hash'; no configuration key selects another layout.

Title: Stored objects are immutable and name-proven
Requirement: No run shall change the bytes at a DataPath that any live manifest row still claims, and shall create a data file only at a content-addressed name that the file's own bytes hash to.
Rationale: The minimal invariant D-1 violated: Mirror addressed data files by PATH while dedup handed that address to rows meaning 'these exact bytes' (defect review 2026-08-24).
AcceptanceCriteria: Across a multi-run timeline that edits one of two duplicate files, a byte census of the pool shows no claimed DataPath whose bytes changed, and the prior snapshot restores the old content for every path that shared it.

Title: Dedup covers content first seen within one run
Requirement: Content with the same (xxH2Hash,Length) appearing several times in a single run shall be stored once, with every logical name referencing that one physical object.
Rationale: D-5: the dedup lookup consulted only the PRIOR backup, so identical files first seen in one run were each stored in full (Mirror) or copied twice over one name (HashAddressed).
AcceptanceCriteria: Two identical files first seen in one run produce exactly one physical pool file, one distinct DataPath across their rows, and one copy/compress operation.

Title: A legacy-form store is refused, not converted or restored
Requirement: The system shall not re-form data already stored: changing CompressEnabled shall govern only content written after the change, leaving existing objects in the form they were stored in. A manifest row recorded in the legacy Original (path-addressed) form shall fail its backup set before any mutation, naming the condition and the remedy (back up to a fresh BackupPath); -Action Verify shall report it as a finding rather than refuse. Both restorers shall apply the same refusal before writing anything: a manifest row carrying StoredAsHashSize='Original', or a DataPath containing a path separator, shall abort the restore with the precondition exit code and no file written. There is no read path for a pre-content-addressed store in this kit.
Rationale: Human rulings 2026-08-25: no store exists that must be maintained (so the Original->Hash conversion is deleted rather than made safe), and retroactive space reclamation - in either direction - is not required (so the compression-flip migration goes with it, to a deferred standalone re-pack script if ever wanted). A mixed-form store is already normal because compression is per-file (SR-004), and every row's Compressed describes its OWN object, so nothing downstream needs re-forming. Deleting the migration also deletes a risk class: every migration is a mass rewrite of a store that currently works. Read support was withdrawn 2026-08-26 (human ruling) rather than left as an untested claim: WP9's independent review found the bash half of 'both restorers still restore a legacy store' had no fixture (MIN-2), and the honest resolution was to drop the promise, not to build a fixture for a capability nobody needs -- no such store is known to exist.
AcceptanceCriteria: Flipping CompressEnabled re-forms no existing object; new content follows the new setting; the mixed-form store restores byte-exact through both restorers and audits CLEAN. A store whose manifest carries StoredAsHashSize='Original' fails -Action Backup with the fresh-BackupPath remedy and nothing staged or mutated, and yields a finding with a non-zero status under -Action Verify. A constructed legacy store is refused by BOTH restorers with exit 2, naming the cause, with nothing written into the restore target.

Title: Generated browse view
Requirement: When BrowseView is 'index' the system shall generate a manifest-derived browse view OUTSIDE both roots - INDEX.tsv always, plus per-folder INDEX.html pages and a root search page - covering every logical path including duplicate siblings, refreshed when the canonical manifest ROWS it mirrors change (a SHA-256 of those rows is stamped into .viewstamp - NOT the manifest witness, because a manifest-identical run can rewrite the file with different CSV quoting) and on -Action View; no engine or restore path shall read it.
Rationale: Replaces Mirror's browsability, which was its only real value (human ruling 2026-08-24; the per-folder scaling shape approved 2026-08-25 after a single flat page was measured at ~100 MB for a 500k-file library).
AcceptanceCriteria: The view's entries equal the manifest's RelativePath set exactly, each named RelativePath+('.7z' when the ROW's Compressed is Yes); a stale row-digest triggers a rebuild; -Action View is idempotent; Verify, prune accounting and both restorers ignore the view entirely.

Title: Configuration contract v2
Requirement: The JSON configuration contract shall declare ConfigVersion 2; PreserveFolderTree shall be refused BY NAME in every configuration format; BrowseView (off|index, with link reserved and refused) and ViewPath shall be accepted, ViewPath refused when it is not on the backup volume, or OVERLAPS any path the set owns - BackupPath, ChangePath, SourcePath or SourceStatePath - in EITHER direction (inside one, equal to one, or containing one). The view generator shall additionally refuse to wipe a view root holding anything that is not a generated view.
Rationale: Mirror is gone, so a stale config must fail loudly rather than be silently reinterpreted. CLIXML is exempt from SR-042's closed schema, so without an explicit refusal PreserveFolderTree there would be silently ignored.
AcceptanceCriteria: A config carrying PreserveFolderTree fails with status 2 naming the key, in BOTH JSON and CLIXML; an out-of-vocabulary BrowseView and each ViewPath placement violation fail by name, including a ViewPath that CONTAINS a storage root or IS the source tree (WP9 review MAJ-1: those shapes deleted the store and the source respectively, on a run that reported success); and a view root holding ordinary user files is refused rather than wiped.

Title: Store audits scale linearly
Requirement: The unreferenced-data-file audit shall be linear in manifest rows plus on-disk data files.
Rationale: Test-BackupManifest re-pipes the whole manifest per on-disk file (O(N^2)) and runs on every backup via Sync step 6; at 500k files it plausibly never finishes.
AcceptanceCriteria: With 10k manifest rows and 10k pool files the audit completes within the harness budget and reports the findings the quadratic implementation reported, with one deliberate difference: existence is decided from the enumerated data-file set, which skips ROOT-LEVEL infrastructure names, so a row whose DataPath is a root-level infrastructure name is blanked rather than kept. No build can produce such a row (the hash-name grammar cannot spell one) and a legacy store is refused first (SR-061), so the case is unreachable rather than merely unlikely.

Title: Empty directories and folder attributes are recorded and restored
Requirement: The system shall record, beside each manifest, one row per source directory that contains no file anywhere beneath it or carries any of the folder attributes Hidden, System, ReadOnly or NotContentIndexed, and both restorers shall recreate those directories and (on Windows) re-apply those attributes after all file content is written and verified. The record shall be advisory: it shall not be witnessed, and an absent, unreadable or malformed record shall leave the pre-existing behaviour and shall never fail a restore. A directory the walk could not enumerate shall not be recorded. On a POSIX host the directories shall be created and the inapplicable attributes reported, not silently dropped.
Rationale: MANIFEST.csv has one row per FILE, so an empty directory was never recreated and a Hidden or System FOLDER came back ordinary (reproduced 2026-08-25, documented in README as a known gap). Ruled 2026-08-26: option B, a small sidecar, limited to the four attribute bits SetFileAttributes can apply to a directory. ReadOnly is included despite meaning nothing about writability on a directory -- it is the flag Explorer reads for a desktop.ini customised view.
AcceptanceCriteria: A backup of a tree containing an empty directory, a nested empty directory and a Hidden+System folder writes a DIRECTORIES.csv naming exactly those three; restoring recreates both empty directories and returns the folder Hidden+System; a tree with no empty or attributed directory writes no sidecar at all and is byte-identical to a pre-SR-065 store; a store whose sidecar is deleted or replaced with garbage still restores every file and exits 0; the bash restorer creates the directories and logs the attributes as not applied; a snapshot carries the sidecar of the state it preserves, not the live one.

Title: Restored files carry their own modification time
Requirement: Both restorers shall apply each restored file's own LastWriteTimeStr from the manifest row it was restored from, after that file has passed its post-write (Length, xxH2Hash) verification. A blank or unparseable value shall be logged and the row shall still count as restored; the timestamp shall never fail a restore.
Rationale: Attributes and timestamps were never applied from the index -- they rode along on the copy -- so every row sharing one deduplicated pool object restored with the timestamp of whichever file created that object. Reproduced 2026-08-25: two identical files dated 2001 and 2002 both came back dated 2001. LastWriteTimeStr was already in the manifest, correct per row, and simply never read by a restorer, so the timestamp half needs no schema change. The attribute half for FILES remains out of contract (README 'What is not recorded').
AcceptanceCriteria: Two files with identical content and different modification times restore with their OWN times under both restorers, in Plain and Compress; a unique file's time is likewise preserved; a row whose LastWriteTimeStr is blank or garbage restores its bytes, warns, and exits 0.

Title: A transiently unreadable source file is retried, not lost
Requirement: A copy or compress that fails for a reason which could change shall be retried after a short delay, up to three attempts per file, bounded by a per-run retry budget shared across the whole set; a failure that cannot change on a retry shall not consume the budget. A file still unreadable when its attempts are exhausted shall be logged as an error naming the attempt count, shall receive NO manifest row for the content that was not stored, and shall mark the set failed. A file that already had a manifest row from an earlier run shall keep that row, which names bytes the store still holds.
Rationale: The SR-060 candidate loop falls back only to other MEMBERS of a content group, so a file whose content is UNIQUE had exactly one attempt: a momentary antivirus, indexer or editor lock cost it the whole run. Human ruling 2026-08-26, after a shortfall-detection guard was rejected as prone to firing on legitimate bulk deletions: the walk at the start of the run is the authority on what must be stored, and a per-file transient is the thing worth retrying. The per-run budget exists because a systemic failure fails deterministically for every file beneath it, and retrying thousands of those would turn a scheduled run into an hours-long sleep (SN-011).
AcceptanceCriteria: A source file held under an exclusive handle released after the first attempt is backed up successfully, with the retry visible in the log; a permanently unreadable file exhausts its three attempts, marks the set failed, and leaves NO row in the manifest; a directory occupying the destination is refused immediately without consuming a retry; a run whose budget is spent stops waiting, says so, and fails the remaining files without sleeping.
